official.deadline_note: Separate deadlines per track: the only round currently open is the Fulbright Specialist Program 2027-28 call for Polish host institutions (6 October 2026 - 8 January 2027). U.S. Student Program 2027-28 applications closed 6 October 2026 (2028-29 cycle launches spring 2027). Polish-citizen awards run on their own windows: Fulbright Graduate Student Award 2027-28 closed 27 April 2026 with the 2028-29 round planned to launch February 2027; Fulbright Junior Research Award applies May-October; Fulbright Polish Scholar Award and STEM Impact Award February-May; Fulbright Polish Studies Award May-September; Fulbright Schuman Award September-December.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 cycle (Specialist Program 2027-28 open 6 Oct 2026 - 8 Jan 2027; U.S. Student Program 2027-28 closed 6 Oct 2026; 2028-29 U.S. cycle launching spring 2027)
official.status_note: The Fulbright Specialist Program 2027-28 call is open from 6 October 2026 to 8 January 2027. The U.S. Student Program 2027-28 competition closed 6 October 2026 with semi-finalist notifications expected by end of January 2027 and the 2028-29 application launching spring 2027. The Commission's Graduate Student Award 2027-28 recruitment (9 February - 27 April 2026) has ended; the next round for academic year 2028-29 is planned to open in February 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: For the Fulbright Graduate Student Award the Commission states the total award of up to 47,000 USD covers monthly living allowances, all one-off allowances and tuition fees: 'czesne' - partial or full coverage of tuition and/or fees required by the host institution, including university health insurance fees, depending on remaining budget funds. Research-only awards (Junior Research, Polish Scholar, STEM Impact) cover living costs and allowances, not tuition.
benefits: Monthly stipend for living expenses (Graduate Student Award 2025-26 examples: 2,831-4,300 USD/month depending on host institution)
Roundtrip travel allowance (Graduate Student Award: 1,500 USD lump sum)
One-off allowances: relocation and settling in (1,300 USD) and conference/study-aid costs (1,000 USD)
J-1 visa and SEVIS fee coverage; Accident and Sickness Program for Exchanges (ASPE) medical insurance meeting J-1 requirements
Additional funding for mandatory host institution fees, relocation, research, conferences and family support (depending on the programme)
Pre-departure orientation, in-grant support, enrichment activities and lifelong membership in the Fulbright alumni community of over 400,000
eligibility: Polish citizenship for grants to the U.S.; U.S. citizenship for grants to Poland - the two tracks are separate competitions
Dual Polish-American citizens, U.S. Green Card holders and individuals residing in the U.S. at the time of application are ineligible for grants to the U.S.
English language proficiency at minimum B2 level (Graduate Student Award); proficiency sufficient for professional communication in an English-speaking academic environment
Meeting formal requirements of a J-1 visa (Polish-citizen track)
Academic excellence and justified need/motivation to study, research or teach in the partner country
Preference for candidates without substantial recent experience in the U.S. (under 9 months in the last 5 years; under 5 years total in the 6 years before applying)

Full electronic application plus the separate country-specific supplementary form, both submitted before the deadline

application_method: Polish citizens: register in the Commission's online application system (apply.iie.org FFSP form), complete all tabs and upload documents, then submit the separate supplementary form (Google Form) before the deadline

U.S. citizens (U.S. Student Program and English Teaching Assistant Awards): apply through the national U.S. Student Program portal us.fulbrightonline.org (application at apply.iie.org/fulbrightusstudent), typically via the campus Fulbright Program Adviser; Poland requires an invitation letter from a Polish host institution (ETA applicants are placed by the Commission and do not need one)
U.S. academics (U.S. Scholar Program): apply through fulbrightscholars.org, with the annual Poland competition running approximately February to mid-September
U.S. specialists: join the global Fulbright Specialist Roster administered by World Learning; Polish institutions initiate Specialist and ETA projects through open competitions run by the Commission
official.application_route: Polish citizens apply via the Commission's online system (apply.iie.org FFSP) plus a mandatory supplementary form; U.S. citizens apply via us.fulbrightonline.org (Student/ETA), fulbrightscholars.org (Scholar) or World Learning (Specialist roster).
official.citizenship_residency: Polish citizenship required for grants to the U.S. (dual Polish-American citizens, U.S. Green Card holders and U.S. residents at time of application are ineligible); U.S. citizenship required for grants to Poland
official.international_eligibility: Open only to Polish citizens (grants to the U.S.) and U.S. citizens (grants to Poland); third-country nationals are not eligible through the Polish-U.S. Fulbright Commission
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All academic disciplines accepted. Graduate Student Award excludes medical studies requiring direct patient contact, LLM and MBA programmes (a separate LL.M award with the University of Notre Dame is offered); research awards exclude projects involving direct patient contact
official.research_requirement: Applicants must present a research, study or teaching project agreed with the host institution and approved by the Commission; letters of invitation from the proposed U.S. host are mandatory for research awards, and U.S. Student Program applicants to Poland must hold an invitation from a Polish institution
official.duration: 3-10 months (U.S. Scholar); 9-10 months (U.S. Student research); 9 months (English Teaching Assistant); 14-42 days / 2-6 weeks (Specialist, STEM Impact); 4-10 months (Junior Research); 3-9 months (Polish Studies); one academic year renewable for a second year (Graduate Student Award)
official.description: The Fulbright Program is a highly competitive, merit-based grant programme for international educational exchange, operating in Poland since 1959 and administered by the Polish-U.S. Fulbright Commission with funding from the Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education and the U.S. Department of State. It funds study, research, teaching and professional exchange in both directions - Polish citizens to the United States and U.S. citizens to Poland - across all academic disciplines and career stages.
official.program_type: Graduate, PhD, Postdoctoral, Teaching, Research, Professional
official.english_requirement: Minimum B2 English level for the Graduate Student Award, evidenced by a current TOEFL, IELTS, CAE, CPE or other B2 certificate (e.g. language-centre certificate or a degree completed in English with transcript); general requirement is English proficiency sufficient for professional communication in an English-speaking academic environment

applicant_utility.summary: Fulbright Poland is two parallel competitions with different calendars: Polish citizens compete for grants to the U.S. (flagship Graduate Student Award, worth up to $47,000 in year one covering tuition, a monthly living stipend of roughly $2,800-$4,300 depending on the host city, travel and insurance), while Americans apply through the national U.S. Student or Scholar competitions for grants to Poland. Right now the only open door is the Specialist Program 2027-28 window for Polish host institutions, closing 8 January 2027, after which attention shifts to the 2028-29 rounds (U.S. Student applications expected to open in spring 2027; the Polish Graduate Student Award in February 2027). Because selection runs through a formal screen, three independent expert reviews, an interview and final approval by the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board and the U.S. Department of State, an application has to be complete and entirely plagiarism-free before the cutoff - incomplete files never reach reviewers.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Polish Master's graduates chasing a U.S. graduate degree or PhD candidates/researchers with a secured U.S. host invitation; U.S. academics and advanced students who already have a concrete Polish host contact
application_readiness_checklist: Line up your host institution invitation early - it is mandatory for research awards and for U.S. students going to Poland, and a vague 'interest' email is not enough
Register your three referees early: recommendation links are issued to their inboxes and you cannot see the letters' content, only their status
Prepare a U.S.-format CV (no photo, birth date or marital status) and a 10-20 page writing sample you solely authored
Get sworn-translated diplomas and transcripts if your university did not issue them in English
Secure a current B2 English certificate (TOEFL, IELTS, CAE, CPE or equivalent) before the window opens
Check the U.S.-presence limits (under 9 months in the last 5 years; under 5 years total in the last 6) before investing months in the application
Diarise the separate supplementary country form - it is an independent submission with the same deadline as the main application
common_rejection_risks: Formal-screen rejection for an incomplete file - the Commission will not pre-check your application for completeness
Any element of plagiarism detected at any stage voids the application irreversibly
A project that could be done anywhere: reviewers score how essential the U.S. (or Poland) and the specific host are to your plan
Naming host institutions in the Study/Research Objective instead of the Study Plan section, or relying on prestige alone as justification
Recommenders submitting after your own submission deadline, leaving the file formally incomplete
Missing or untranslated diplomas, an expired English certificate, or forgetting the supplementary form
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Self-placement route university application fees plus GRE/TOEFL costs (the IIE-placed route covers these), J-2 dependent visa costs and family medical insurance (ASPE does not cover dependants), any costs above the 47,000 USD cap, and PhD funding after the grant's second year, which depends on a host-department RA/TA offer
document_audit: Diplomas and transcripts not issued in English need a sworn translator, or a translator's version stamped by the dean's office - upload both original and translation
A published writing sample must be sole-authored; prefer peer-reviewed work or an original chapter/term paper in your field's citation style (MLA, APA, CSE, Chicago)
Recommendation letters are blind to you - verify their submitted status in the portal before the deadline rather than asking referees for copies
Applicants already admitted to U.S. studies must add the official admission letter and the university's written deferral consent to academic year 2027-28
The supplementary Google Form is separate from the main application system; submitting one does not submit the other
alerts: The U.S. Student Program 2027-28 cycle closed on 6 October 2026 - the next window opens in spring 2027, so start preparing host letters now
Fulbright Specialist Program 2027-28 for Polish institutions is open 6 October 2026 - 8 January 2027; projects can name a specialist or request a match from the global roster
J-1 grantees are subject to the two-year home-country physical presence requirement after the grant

Polish Fulbright scholarships are exempt from Polish income tax (art. 21.1 pt 39d), and family reunification on J-2 requires proof of additional funds (~50% of the stipend for the first dependant, 25% for each further one)
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in the Commission's/IIE online system, complete every tab and upload all documents, submit the separate country-specific supplementary form by the cutoff, then pass formal and anti-plagiarism screening, three expert field reviews, an online interview and Commission Board recommendation for final Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board and U.S. Department of State approval - after which admitted grantees proceed through IIE-placed or self-placed university applications
